# I. CONTEXT

Ituri Province is located in the North-East of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and shares a long border with Uganda and South Sudan.
For more than two decades, it has been facing a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent population displacements.
It has an estimated population of over 8 million inhabitants, including more than one million internally displaced persons.

In September 2018, this province was affected by an Ebola virus disease epidemic that was raging in the neighbouring province of Nord-Kivu.

The Mongbwalu health zone is one of the 36 health zones of Ituri province.
Considered the starting point of the epidemic, it is located in Djugu territory where several armed groups operate.
It is located 70 km from Bunia, capital of Ituri province, with frequent population movements towards Uganda.
This locality has the particularity of having several mining sites that attract populations coming from other territories of the province and neighbouring provinces.

# II. HISTORY OF THE EPIDEMIC

On 05 May 2026, social networks reported a spike in deaths of unknown cause with nearly 50 deaths already recorded in the Mongbwalu health zone.
Following confirmation of this alert, the Chief Medical Officer of the Mongbwalu health zone shared the preliminary investigation report on 09 May 2026.
On 11 May 2026, the provincial health authorities organised an emergency meeting and decided to deploy rapid response teams to Mongbwalu and to Rwampara, which had reported suspected deaths from viral haemorrhagic fever among patients hospitalised at the Centre médical Evangélique of Rwampara, originating from Mongbwalu.

Investigations conducted on 12 May 2026, simultaneously in the Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones by the Rapid Intervention Teams of the Provincial Health Division (DPS) of Ituri revealed that most suspected patients or deaths presented with fever, headache, vomiting, and severe physical asthenia.
Deaths occurred 2 to 3 days after disease onset in a clinical picture of haematemesis, epistaxis, or blackish vomiting.
During the investigations in the Rwampara health zone, 20 samples were taken from suspected cases or deaths.
The majority of people sampled originated from the Mongbwalu health zone.
Preliminary tests performed at the Bunia Laboratory were all negative for Ebola Zaire, dengue, Rotavirus, Cholera, Malaria, Yersinia pestis, mpox, and COVID-19.
These samples were sent to the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) in Kinshasa for additional examinations.

On 14 May 2026, 13 cases of these 20 samples were tested and 8 were positive for non-Zaire Ebola virus disease at INRB Kinshasa.
On 15 May 2026, sequencing of the positive samples enabled the identification of the BUNDIBUGYO strain, which enabled the Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare (MSHPS) to officially declare the 17th Ebola virus disease epidemic.

Ebola virus disease (Bundibugyo strain), thus marking the 17th epidemic in the country's history

On 17 May 2026, in consultation with member states, the Director-General of WHO considered that the event taking place in the DRC and Uganda meets the criteria of the definition set out in Article 1 of the IHR, and declared that this constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, while specifying that the risk at the global level is low but high at the regional level.

On 18 May 2026, the Director General of Africa CDC officially declared a public health emergency of continental security (PHECS) under Article 3 of its statutes.
This declaration followed an emergency meeting of the Africa CDC consultative group, which considered that the worsening epidemic posed an acute risk to continental health security.
Consequently, the Continental Incident Management Support Team was activated to provide support to affected Member States and those at risk, in terms of response and preparedness.

# IV. RESPONSE ACTIONS

## COORDINATION

● Holding of a coordination meeting chaired by the Deputy Incident Manager, Head of the Provincial Health Division of Nord-Kivu (Beni) and Ituri (Bunia).
● Holding of the partner mobilisation meeting on alignment with the response plan.
● Development of the provincial Ebola Virus Disease incident action plan in DPS Ituri and Nord-Kivu.

## EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SURVEILLANCE

● Transmission to the coordination of Terms of Reference for the deployment of multidisciplinary provincial teams to the Mongbwalu ZS.
● Transmission to the coordination of TOR for the training of actors (ECZS, IT&ITA, leads of community workers, and data managers) from five active ZS
● Provision of infrared thermometers in the Nizi ZS (4)

## RISK COMMUNICATION AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT (RCCE)

• Advocacy with the burgomasters of the communes of SHARI, NYAKASANZA and MBUNYA to secure their engagement in support of communication activities for the MVE response advocacy
• Briefing of 19 service heads operating at Bunia airport, including 15 men and 4 women, on MVE and prevention measures in public areas
• Sensitisation of 38 livestock farmers and wholesale cattle dealers at the industrial slaughterhouse of Bunia on preventive measures against MVE, including 16 women and 22 men.
• Educational talk with 30 women during a CPS session on preventive measures against MVE, Bunia ZS, BIGO AS (health area)

## INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL

Bunia ZS
▪ 3 SDB conducted (HGR Bunia (general referral hospital), Rwankole, Bunia-Cite) out of 4 alert cases;
▪ Briefing of healthcare providers in 2 ESS (CSR Bunia-cité and Clinique Universelle) on Waste Management;
▪ Briefing of 3 teams (Bunia ZS and Rwampara ZS) on safe and dignified burial (SDB);
▪ Briefing of 9 providers by EMIR on triage and isolation, waste management, active search in ESS, and injection safety

Rwampara ZS
▪ Briefing of 20 providers on donning and doffing of PPE, waste disposal, decontamination, and handwashing (HGR-Rwampara).
▪ Surface decontamination at CME Nyakunde, intensive care at HGR Rwampara, and the isolation ward.
▪ 3 SDB conducted out of 4 alert cases (1 body retrieved by the family);
▪ Decontamination in 20 households around the case.

Mongbwalu ZS
- Decontamination of the HGR MONGBWALU ambulance.
- On-the-spot briefing of 36 hygienists (with the support of PTF) on donning and doffing of PPE

NYAKUNDE ZS
- Decontamination of a household in MARABO and boarding school IEM Nyakunde.

DPS Nord Kivu
• Decontamination of Matanda Hospital where the confirmed case from the Katwa ZS is staying;
• PCI (infection prevention and control) scorecard evaluation of Matanda Hospital: 70,6%;
• Implementation of case mapping;
• Assessment of the CTE to identify PCI input needs (PPE, handwashing facilities, chlorine, waste management, patient pathway).

## LOGISTICS

❖ Delivery of inputs and protective equipment to the laboratory and PCI pillars for 4 Category 1 ESS (HGR Bunia, HGR Rwampara, CH SALAMA and CH CME
❖ Delivery of inputs and protective equipment to the LITA ZS for SDB
❖ Unpacking of inputs and equipment received as of 21 May 2026
❖ Monitoring of installation work of care tents at HGR Bunia (ALIMA and WHO) and installation of the CTE in Mongbwalu by MSF

## HOLISTIC CARE

• Briefing of providers at HGR Bunia and Rwampara on wearing PPE;
• Clinical evaluation of patients;
• Dispatch of 5 mattresses, 5 beds and other materials to CME
• Finalisation of statement of needs with WFP.
• Clinical evaluation of patients;
• On-the-spot briefing of 10 providers on clinical management;
• Monitoring of erection of two isolation tents at HGR Bunia, of which one is ready and the other in progress;

## SECURITY

• The security situation in the city of Bunia (Bunia and Rwampara ZS) is relatively calm
• Security briefing for deployed teams.

# V. CHALLENGES

● Lack of standardised CT (transit centre) and CTE
● Shortage of PCI materials (PPE, handwashing facilities, chlorine) in Nord Kivu
● Low transmission of alerts by zones;
● Delay in sample collection;
● Lack of nutritional support;
● Absence of psychosocial interventions in Mongbwalu;
● Delay in setting up isolation sites.

# VI. Recommendation

● Make operational the CT and CTE of Beni, Butembo and Goma (rehabilitation and review of patient flow)
● Strengthen surveillance with a view to escalating alerts and tracing contacts never seen and lost to follow-up;
● Mobilise resources to support the different pillars of the response;
● Training of providers on surveillance in MVE and in SBC in affected and high-risk ZS;
● Training of Community Health Workers on surveillance in MVE and in SBC in affected and high-risk ZS.
